solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fit to hang, feu being exercised? It could clobber distant felon

indicators.note: letters being exercised are put through their paces and moved about into a new order

parts.note: all twelve letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A feudal tenure being used to justify a hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTFANGTHIEF was a medieval lord's right to pursue a thief beyond his own land and bring him back for judgment. The definition is a playful description of that right.
explanation.definitionFit: The old legal privilege let a lord seize and punish a criminal caught outside his own jurisdiction, so it could indeed punish a remote wrongdoer.

clue.text: Watchdog 'ad position in chair, fine inside

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of 'ad tells you to drop an H from the matching word
inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: had position in chair is hosted, with the aitch dropped
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An inspector who chaired a panel, with a fine thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hosted, said with a dropped H as in 'ad, gives OSTED; insert F after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofsted is the UK government body that inspects schools, a regulatory watchdog.

clue.text: Responding to stimulus, I mostly remain after drink's served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: Someone lingering at the bar after a round is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts I and the shortened STICK behind the reversed drink; the 's stands for has.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropistic describes an organism turning towards or away from a stimulus, as plants do towards light.

clue.text: Obsession one's trapped by was effective endlessly

indicators.note: trapped by puts the first piece inside the following word
endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: fetch can mean to take effect or succeed
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An obsession that once worked has someone trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim FETCHED to FETCHE, then put I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetiche is an old spelling of fetish, an object of irrational devotion or obsession.

clue.text: Denial of liability in brief letter left involving children

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the first pieces wrap round the last

parts.note: a note is a short letter
L is the abbreviation for left
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A short note left in a family's name disowning responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief letter' looks like a short message disowning debts, which is apt, since a notchel was published as just such a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A notchel is a public notice that one will not pay another person's debts, a repudiation of liability.

clue.text: Old-style fourpenny one's attack catching Bunter's rear

indicators.note: catching means grabbing hold of, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: go at means attack

indicators.note: the rear of a name is its final letter

parts.note: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of British comic stories

explanation.surface: A clip round the ear for the fat schoolboy Billy Bunter's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: A fourpenny one is British slang for a punch, which makes the surface a fight; here it is read literally as a coin worth four old pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The groat was an old English silver coin worth fourpence.

clue.text: Representative showing selection of pretty pictures

indicators.note: a selection of the following words is shown, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the run starts within the first word and ends within the second

explanation.surface: A sample of pretty pictures as a representative showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Typic is an old word for typical, serving as a representative example.

clue.text: Holy place I do out in straw

indicators.note: out means left out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a halidom is a holy place or sanctuary
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: Someone tidying straw out of a sacred place.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I DO from HALIDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Halm is a variant of haulm, the stalks or stems of plants used as straw.

clue.text: Pen's translated Irish Gaelic? It exists purely in the mind

definitions.text: It exists purely in the mind

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters change places

parts.note: anagram fodder
Erse is the old name for Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A writer's work rendered into Irish, with a doubt about whether it is real.
explanation.walkthrough: Ens per se is a Latin philosophical phrase, run together in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ens per se is a being existing in itself, in philosophy a pure entity conceived only in thought.

clue.text: A stone inset by fashionable American firmly (old)

indicators.note: inset by means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: fly is slang for smart or stylish, especially in the US
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A gem set firmly into a trendy American jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastly is an obsolete adverb meaning firmly or securely.

clue.text: Con, after running free, in shrine

indicators.note: something running is in motion, so the letters move into another order

parts.note: anagram fodder
Con. is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A convict, having escaped, hides in a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a prisoner, but it is the Conservative abbreviation; 'after' puts the mixed-up FREE first.
explanation.definitionFit: A feretory is a portable or fixed reliquary chapel holding a saint's relics, a kind of shrine.

clue.text: Source of ghee? You'll find this is used in Asian recipe

indicators.note: this word plus 'is' are used up in the jumbled source letters, a composite mixing of letters
you find the answer by taking the word 'is' away from the longer mixed group

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription
taken as written, and removed from the letters

explanation.surface: A cookery note about ghee being an ingredient in Asian dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus IS shuffled together give the letters of ASIAN and R. Remove IS from ASIANR and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The arna is the wild water buffalo of India, whose milk can be made into ghee.

clue.text: Soak imbibing litre in bar…;

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a soak is a drunkard
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A drunk downing a litre in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be the pub; it is the definition, a bolt or bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a slot is also a bar or bolt, as used to fasten a door.

clue.text: …Soak similarly drunk with slops meant to minimize wastage?

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and staggers, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: as in the previous clue, a soak is a drunkard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk lapping up slops so that nothing goes to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Similarly' tells you to read Soak the same way as in the clue before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-loss order or measure is designed to limit losses, a way of minimising waste.

clue.text: Pudding, alternative to pie in a covering, rolled round

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
rolled round means turned the other way about, so the covering is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a coat is a covering, as of paint
in printing, pi is an alternative spelling of pie, jumbled type

explanation.surface: A dessert where pie is swapped for something wrapped in pastry and rolled.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse A COAT, then insert PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy pudding made from cassava.

clue.text: Morgan maybe having to exhibit evidence of injury (9, two words)

parts.note: to sport is to wear or show off
a scar is the mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: A person named Morgan who must show wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Morgan is a British maker of hand-built sports cars, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A Morgan is an example of a sports car, signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Bushy plant amateur removed from Uncle Sam

indicators.note: removed from tells you to take letters out of the following word

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA
AM is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: An amateur gardener ousted from the USA with a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AM from AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the genus of heaths, low bushy evergreen shrubs.

clue.text: Light car leaked fluid around autobahn

parts.note: dye or paint that has run has leaked fluid
German motorways are numbered with an A, like A7
'bout is short for about, meaning around

explanation.surface: A small car leaking oil on a German motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: 'around' may be ABOUT on its own, with autobahn only scene-setting, or 'BOUT plus A for the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A runabout is a small light car for short trips.

clue.text: Goldsmith's vessel made of copper I can cut from alembic

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: cut from means sliced out of the word that follows

parts.note: a pelican is a kind of alembic, a distilling vessel
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: A goldsmith making a vessel from copper cut out of a still.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican was an alchemist's alembic with a beak-like neck; take I CAN from it to leave PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupel is a small porous dish used in assaying gold and silver.

clue.text: Troubled type makes case for it before submitting formal request

indicators.note: a case surrounds what it holds, so the mixed letters go round the rest
troubled letters are disturbed and fall into another order

parts.note: anagram fodder
taken as written
or is an archaic word for before, as in 'or ever'

explanation.surface: A worried person builds an argument before making a formal petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a time word linking the halves; it is the archaic or, as in 'or ever', and goes in the case too.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitory means petitioning, making a formal request or claim.

clue.text: Oily pastes from sea fish containing measure of fluid

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: tai are Japanese sea breams
the hin is an ancient Hebrew liquid measure

explanation.surface: Fish oils being processed into paste.
explanation.walkthrough: The tai is a Japanese sea bream and the hin a measure from the Old Testament, both Chambers staples.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is an oily paste made from ground sesame seeds.

clue.text: 'Turkish delight'? Watchful when it comes up to grab centre of that!

indicators.note: to grab means to seize and hold, so one piece encloses the other
in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: alert means watchful

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the central pair of a four-letter word

explanation.surface: Keeping a close eye on a sweet treat ready to snatch it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks on 'Turkish delight' warn that it is not the confection but a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Trehala, or Turkish manna, is a sweet substance from insect cocoons eaten in Turkey, a delicacy from that land.

clue.text: Place between Tay and liner at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the fodder, with 'and' joining the two words

explanation.surface: A ship positioned between the River Tay estuary and the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a Scottish river; 'and' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlay is to lay or insert something between other layers.

clue.text: Like wee one belonging to a besotted Mrs

parts.note: in can mean belonging to, as in a member in a club

indicators.note: besotted means fuddled or infatuated, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A baby that belongs to a doting mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Besotted' paints a doting mother, but it only scrambles the letters of Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby too young to walk is carried in the arms, so in arms describes a wee one.

clue.text: Plant fibres nursed by botanist Leschenault

indicators.note: nursed by means cradled within the following words

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A botanist cultivating plant fibres.
explanation.walkthrough: Leschenault was a French botanist, which makes the hidden word easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong fibre from Mexican agave and yucca plants, used for cordage.

clue.text: Wild Asian water plants

indicators.note: wild means unruly and out of control, so the letters run riot

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Plants growing wild in Asian waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Naias is a genus of submerged freshwater plants, the water nymphs.

clue.text: Since old, presiding over English faculty

parts.note: sens is an old word for since
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A long-serving head chairing the English faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, presiding over puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense such as sight or hearing is one of the body's faculties of perception.

clue.text: Hot and very dry around watercourse, shallow

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: so means very
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
TT is teetotal, a dry person

explanation.surface: A shallow stream in a hot and very arid land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very dry' wants to be one idea; very and dry are separate pieces. The parse is uncertain, and the definition stretches watercourse to cover a marshy lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A shott is a shallow salt lake or marsh in North Africa, fed by seasonal water.

clue.text: Honours school half-heartedly?

indicators.note: only half the heart is kept, so one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: Fettes College is a well-known Edinburgh boarding school

explanation.surface: A school that awards honours only grudgingly.
explanation.walkthrough: FETTES has a double T at its centre; halving that heart leaves one T.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or celebrate them lavishly.

clue.text: Classical township is wiped out in the end

indicators.note: wiped out in means erased from within the following word

parts.note: demise is death, the end
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: An ancient town eventually destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of DEMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deme was a township or local division of ancient Attica.

clue.text: Cracking eight's about No. 1 in Henley, pre-eminently placed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
something cracking is breaking up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe-s read as a plural

indicators.note: number one in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Henley is the Thames rowing regatta

explanation.surface: A rowing eight at Henley Regatta in top form, placed first.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a famous rowing event on the Thames where eights race.
explanation.definitionFit: High-set means set or placed high, so in an exalted position.

clue.text: Saw inside their eggs what may be fatal for fish

definitions.text: what may be fatal for fish

indicators.note: inside places the first piece within the second

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
short for tenon saw, a fine-toothed carpenter's saw

explanation.surface: Someone noticing poison inside fish eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is a tool, the tenon saw. 'Their' refers back to the fish in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotenone is a plant-derived pesticide used to kill fish in water management.

clue.text: Amateur given saddle in system leading to contracts?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for amateur
a col is a saddle between two peaks; 'given' adds it

explanation.surface: A novice rider getting a saddle as part of a training system.
explanation.walkthrough: Acol is a bidding system in bridge, where the auction ends in a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge bidding systems such as Acol are how partners arrive at a contract to make tricks.

clue.text: Masquerade displaying fizz

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to act in a ...' play or go in disguise, an old spelling of mum
second meaning: a brand of champagne

explanation.walkthrough: Mumm is a Reims champagne house; fizz is slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives mumm as a variant of mum, to masquerade or act in dumb show, and the trade name is a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Stand for casks badly stored in shelf

indicators.note: stored in puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a stage can be a shelf or raised platform
ill means badly

explanation.surface: Barrels poorly packed on a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelf' is a stage in the sense of a raised platform or ledge, such as a microscope's.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillage is a frame or stand on which barrels are set in a cellar.

clue.text: Strong teamsters organized in wily Chicago-style know-how (12, two words)

parts.note: str. is a dictionary abbreviation for strong

indicators.note: organized means arranged in an orderly new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Tough union truck drivers organised by Chicago mobsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Teamsters are US truck drivers, whose union had notorious Chicago links; Chicago-style flags an Americanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Street smarts is American slang for the shrewdness needed to survive in a tough city.
